title: 3.2 · What does the data say? (Claims, predictions, models)
name: What does the data say? (Claims, predictions, models)
summary: Students use charts to back up a claim or a prediction, and learn that sometimes the right answer is: we can't tell yet. In Data Detective's Clues & Claims they mark claims supported, not supported or can't tell yet, and predict the next bar with a slider. Pairs share one device.
iCan: use data to support a claim or a prediction
say when there is not enough data to tell yet
materials: Paper Predictions kit (one die and one tally sheet per pair, for the twin or the block day)
doNow: It rained the last 3 Mondays. Will it rain next Monday? Write yes or no and how sure you are.
plan: Explore: The Plant Race, then a chart with only two days

warmup.why: two retrieval items from 3.1, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from 3.1

do: Open Data Detective at Clues & Claims on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Case 1 is The Plant Race: one bar for each day, and the plant grows about the same amount every day. Ask the class to predict day 10, move the slider to the class guess and check it.
Draw a chart with only two bars on the board, day 1 and day 2. Ask the question below.
say: A claim is something we say is true. Evidence is the data that backs it up.
A claim needs enough good data behind it. Sometimes the right answer is: we can't tell yet.
ask: With only two days, can we tell how tall the plant will be on day 10? What would we need?
explore.afterAsk: Take answers until someone says we need more days. Write Can't tell yet next to the two bars: in today's game that is a real answer, and choosing it at the right time solves the case.
explore.bigIdea: A claim needs enough good data behind it.

play.pairs: driver and navigator on one device; the Swap! banner shows every 3 cases; the navigator reads each claim out loud and points to the bar that backs it up before the driver taps
lookFors: choosing supported for a claim that sounds true but that the chart does not show
never choosing can't tell yet, even when there are only one or two bars
reading the extra column that has nothing to do with the question (cases 5-6)
play.misconception: A claim is not right because it sounds true: it is supported only when the data on the screen shows it, and with too little data the honest answer is can't tell yet.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: Which case tricked you? Why was can't tell yet the right answer?
Think back to the Do Now. Is three rainy Mondays enough data to be sure about next Monday?
showMe: One pair shows the case that tricked them on the projector; the class points to the bar that decides it, or says what data is missing.

exit.sentencePrompt: Pick a chart from today. What does it say, and what do you predict will come next?
exit.frame: The chart says ___, so I predict ___.

rubric.line: Claims and predictions: backing them up with data
levels: Makes a claim or a prediction
Makes a prediction and names the data that backs it up
Also says how sure they are, or when there would not be enough data to tell

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: claim tiles with pictures on cases 1-3
read-aloud on; the navigator reads each claim tile before the driver taps
hint 1 asks: where on the chart do you see that?
stretch: cases 5-6 have an extra column that does not matter; pairs say which column to ignore before they choose
pairs write a claim of their own for case 6 and trade it with a neighbor pair to judge

unpluggedTwin.title: Paper Predictions
materials: a tally sheet with the numbers 1 to 6
grid paper for a bar chart
steps: Pairs roll the die 10 times and make a tally mark for each roll.
They turn the tallies into a bar chart on grid paper.
Predict: before rolling 10 more times, each pair writes which number they think will come up most, and how sure they are.
Roll 10 more, add to the chart and compare with the prediction. Was 10 rolls enough to tell?
Share: which pairs changed their mind after 20 rolls? Write one claim the whole class's data supports.

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: it rained the last 3 Mondays; will it rain next Monday, and how sure are you?

Play Data Detective, chapter Clues & Claims, in pairs for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 3 1 0 0. Goal: 4 cases. No warm-up and no projector needed; sign in with the login cards so the work is saved (signed out is fine only if the cards are missing). No devices or no internet? Run the unplugged twin printed below (Paper Predictions, 15 minutes), then talk about the two discussion questions for 5 minutes.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: Which case tricked you? Why was can't tell yet the right answer?
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut

add: the Paper Predictions twin (15 minutes) before Play
the 3-star stretch and the extra-column cases after Play
10 minutes of chapter Chart It (quest code 2 1 0 0) for pairs who finish

notes: Can't tell yet is a correct answer in this chapter; praise it out loud when a pair chooses it for the right reason.
Most pairs reach case 4 or 5 of 6 in 18 minutes: that is success.
Shared devices: this is an even lesson in the unit, so partner B signs in; the gradebook and the Standards tab count the signed-in student.
